title: BECE English Studies: Grammar & Structure - English Studies - Subject-Verb Agreement
subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Choose the verb that correctly completes the sentence:
"Neither the principal nor the teachers _____ present at the meeting."
questions.explain: According to the rule of proximity, when compound subjects are joined by 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the subject closest to it. Since 'teachers' is plural, the plural verb 'were' is correct.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Complete the sentence with the correct verb:
"The jury _____ divided in their opinions."
questions.explain: When a collective noun indicates divided actions or focuses on individual members—signaled here by the plural pronoun 'their'—it takes a plural verb. Hence, 'are' is the correct verb.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate verb form:
"Everyone in the class _____ submitted the assignment."
questions.explain: Indefinite pronouns such as 'everyone', 'each', 'anyone', and 'someone' are singular and require singular verbs. Therefore, 'has' is correct.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Select the correct verb form for the sentence below:
"Rice and beans _____ my favorite meal."
questions.explain: When two subjects joined by 'and' refer to a single idea, unit, or dish (like rice and beans as one meal), a singular verb is required.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Choose the correct verb to complete the sentence:
"The manager, as well as his two assistants, _____ attending the seminar."
questions.explain: When words such as 'as well as', 'along with', or 'in addition to' join subjects, the verb agrees with the primary (first) subject. Since 'The manager' is singular, the singular verb 'is' is correct.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate verb:
"Fifty thousand naira _____ too much to pay for that simple bag."
questions.explain: Nouns denoting a specific amount of money, a period of time, or distance are considered as a single unit and therefore take a singular verb ('is').
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Select the correct verb for the following sentence:
"He is one of the players who _____ selected for the national team."
questions.explain: In sentences with the structure 'one of the [plural noun] who/that', the relative pronoun (who) refers back to the plural noun (players). Therefore, it requires a plural verb: 'were'.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Which verb correctly completes the sentence?
"A pair of scissors _____ left on the table."
questions.explain: While 'scissors' is inherently plural, the phrasing 'A pair of' acts as a singular collective subject. Therefore, the singular verb 'is' (or 'was') must be used.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Complete the sentence with the correct verb form:
"A number of students _____ absent from class today."
questions.explain: The phrase 'A number of' is plural and means 'several' or 'many', therefore it requires a plural verb ('are'). Conversely, 'The number of' is singular.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Select the correct verb to complete the sentence:
"The news he brought yesterday _____ surprisingly good."
questions.explain: The word 'news' looks plural but is an uncountable noun. Because the sentence mentions 'yesterday', we require a singular verb in the past tense: 'was'.
questions.subject: English Studies
